proofs.proof_tex:
The exact three-snapshot compatibility certificate, torsor classification, local dimensions, zero-displacement elbow, and supermodel transfer are proved in \(\text{thm:three-snapshot-exact-classification}\).  In particular, when \(d_0\ne0\) the dimension is \((p-1)(p-2)/2\), which is positive for \(p\ge3\); since \(d_0\ne0\) is generic in the mean parameter, this proves the three-snapshot assertion in the present theorem.

We prove the four-snapshot assertion directly from the observable equations.  By \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), \(H_0,H_1,H_2\) are positive definite and hence invertible.  If \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\), then \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\succ0\) implies \(\operatorname{rank}(W)=p\), so \(W\) is invertible.  Using both covariance congruences in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_1W
 &=H_2H_1^{-1}W\\
 &=(WH_1W^{\mathsf T})(WH_0W^{\mathsf T})^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1W^{\mathsf T}W^{-\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}W^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1H_0^{-1}=WM_0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The mean equation in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\) is \(d_1=Wd_0\).  The intertwining identity therefore gives, by induction on \(j\),
\[
 M_1^jd_1=M_1^jWd_0=WM_0^jd_0
 \qquad(0\le j<p).
\]
Taking these vectors as columns yields the observable identity
\[
 K_1=WK_0.
\]
Consequently, on the cyclic chart \(\det K_0\ne0\), every raw candidate equals
\[
 W=K_1K_0^{-1}=\mathcal K((m_k),(C_k)).
\]
In particular the true transition satisfies \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\), and there can be at most one raw, hence at most one admissible, transition.

We now prove that the cyclic chart is generic rather than assume it.  Choose pairwise distinct numbers \(v_i\in(0,1)\), and set
\[
 V=\operatorname{diag}(v_1,\ldots,v_p),\qquad
 G=h^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\log v_1,\ldots,\log v_p),\qquad
 \Sigma=I_p,\qquad E=I_p.
\]
Choose \(u=\mu_0-x^\star\) with every coordinate nonzero.  This generator is real, Hurwitz, and in the principal alias strip, and its transition is \(V\).  The latent covariance at snapshot \(j\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(v_i^{2j})\), so common-noise cancellation gives
\[
 H_j=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(v_i^{2j}(1-v_i^2)\bigr)\succ0
 \qquad(j=0,1,2),
\]
and therefore
\[
 M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(v_1^2,\ldots,v_p^2).
\]
The affine mean recursion gives
\[
 d_0=(V-I_p)u,
\]
whose coordinates are all nonzero.  The \(i\)-th row of \(K_0\) is
\[
 d_{0i}(1,v_i^2,\ldots,v_i^{2(p-1)}),
\]
so the Vandermonde determinant calculation gives
\[
 \det K_0
 =\left(\prod_{i=1}^p d_{0i}\right)
 \prod_{1\le i<j\le p}(v_j^2-v_i^2)\ne0.
\]
The displayed choice also has recovered noise \(E=I_p\succ0\), so it belongs to the strict admissible parameter domain.

In general, in coordinates \((V,\Sigma,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\), the entries of \(H_j\) and \(d_j\) are polynomial, while the entries of \(M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}\) are rational with denominators that are powers of \(\det H_0\).  Hence \(\det K_0\) is rational on the domain \(\det H_0\ne0\).  Clearing its nonzero denominator produces a polynomial numerator.  The preceding admissible example makes this numerator nonzero, so it is not the zero polynomial.  Its zero set is a proper algebraic subset.  To record the genericity claim explicitly, induction on the number of scalar coordinates shows that the zero set of a nonzero real polynomial has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero: view the polynomial as a polynomial in the last coordinate, apply the one-dimensional finite-root fact where a coefficient is nonzero, and apply the induction hypothesis to the common zero set of its coefficients.  Thus \(\det K_0\ne0\) off a proper algebraic subset of the admissible parameter domain.

On that complement the rational map recovers the only raw candidate.  If it passes the stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and recovered-noise positivity filters in \(\text{def:admissible-fiber}\), then \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is its singleton.  The bijection of \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) then identifies \(G\), the latent initial covariance, the common measurement covariance, the equilibrium, and \(\mu_0=m_0\).  If the candidate fails a filter, no admissible explanation exists.  This proves the four-snapshot generic identification claim while keeping the structural target distinct from the observable rational recovery map.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(p\ge 2\) and \(H_0,H_1\succ0\).  The three-snapshot raw fiber \(\mathcal F_3\) is nonempty if and only if
\[
 \lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2.
\]
When this equality holds, put \(r=\operatorname{rank}(H_0^{-1/2}d_0)\in\{0,1\}\).  Under the bijection
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2},
\]
the fiber is noncanonically a torsor for \(O(p-r)\), and its dimension is
\[
 \frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}{2}.
\]
Its intersection with the strict filter set
\[
 \left\{W:\rho(W)<1,\ \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,\ C_0-T_W\succ0\right\}
\]
is relatively open.  Consequently every nonempty local admissible branch or stratum has that same dimension.  If \(d_0\ne0\), then \(r=1\), so three snapshots have continuous local ambiguity for \(p\ge3\).  If \(d_0=0\), nonemptiness is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), the fiber is a torsor for \(O(p)\), and continuous ambiguity occurs already at \(p=2\).  These failures of transition identification transfer to every unknown-common-measurement-covariance model whose model class contains the present stable, embeddable, deterministic Gaussian class as a subclass and has the same transition target.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) are positive definite by \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), their symmetric positive-definite square roots and inverse square roots exist.  Define
\[
 a=H_0^{-1/2}d_0,\qquad c=H_1^{-1/2}d_1,
 \qquad U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The inverse change of variables is
\[
 W=H_1^{1/2}UH_0^{-1/2},
\]
so it is a bijection on \(\mathbb R^{p\times p}\).  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1
 &\iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0W^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}=I_p\\
 &\iff UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\\
 &\iff U\in O(p),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equivalence uses that \(U\) is square: \(UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\) makes \(U\) invertible and hence also gives \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_p\).  Likewise,
\[
 Wd_0=d_1
 \iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}H_0^{-1/2}d_0=H_1^{-1/2}d_1
 \iff Ua=c.
\]
Thus \(\text{def:three-fiber}\) yields the exact observable representation
\[
 \mathcal F_3\longleftrightarrow\{U\in O(p):Ua=c\}.
\]

If this set is nonempty, orthogonality gives
\[
 \lVert c\rVert_2^2=c^{\mathsf T}c
 =a^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}Ua
 =a^{\mathsf T}a
 =\lVert a\rVert_2^2,
\]
which proves necessity of the displayed norm equality.  Conversely, suppose \(\lVert a\rVert_2=\lVert c\rVert_2\).  If this common norm is zero, then \(a=c=0\), and every \(U\in O(p)\) is a solution.  If the common norm is positive, extend \(a/\lVert a\rVert_2\) and \(c/\lVert c\rVert_2\) to orthonormal bases of \(\mathbb R^p\).  The orthogonal map sending the first basis to the second sends \(a\) to \(c\).  This proves sufficiency without any unobserved condition.

Fix one solution \(U_0\).  For any other solution \(U\), set \(R_0=U_0^{\mathsf T}U\).  Then
\[
 R_0\in O(p),\qquad R_0a=U_0^{\mathsf T}c=a,
 \qquad U=U_0R_0.
\]
Conversely, every \(R_0\in O(p)\) satisfying \(R_0a=a\) gives the solution \(U_0R_0\), and the representation is unique.  Hence the solution set is a torsor for the stabilizer
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}(a)=\{R_0\in O(p):R_0a=a\}.
\]
If \(a=0\), this stabilizer is \(O(p)\).  If \(a\ne0\), the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^p=\operatorname{span}(a)\oplus a^\perp
\]
shows that every stabilizer element is the identity on \(\operatorname{span}(a)\) and an arbitrary orthogonal map on \(a^\perp\); hence it is isomorphic to \(O(p-1)\).  Since a nonzero column vector has rank one, these two cases are exactly \(O(p-r)\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(a)\in\{0,1\}\).

For completeness, the dimension formula follows locally rather than from a dimension count asserted by name.  At the identity, differentiating \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_s\) gives
\[
 Z^{\mathsf T}+Z=0.
\]
The free entries of a skew-symmetric \(s\times s\) matrix are its \(s(s-1)/2\) entries strictly above the diagonal.  An explicit local chart is the Cayley map
\[
 Z\longmapsto (I_s-Z)(I_s+Z)^{-1}.
\]
For \(Z^{\mathsf T}=-Z\) sufficiently near zero, direct multiplication shows that this matrix is orthogonal.  Conversely, for an orthogonal \(Q\) sufficiently near \(I_s\), the inverse formula
\[
 Z=(I_s-Q)(I_s+Q)^{-1}
\]
is defined and is skew-symmetric.  Thus this is a bijective local coordinate map, and left translation supplies the same chart at every group element.  Taking \(s=p-r\) proves
\[
 \dim\mathcal F_3=\dim O(p-r)=\frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}2.
\]

We next justify that the dimension is the dimension of the structural, rather than merely algebraic, ambiguity.  Let \(W\in\mathcal F_3\) satisfy the three strict filters in the statement.  Since \(\rho(W)<1\), Jordan normal form gives constants \(A<\infty\) and \(b\in(0,1)\) such that \(\lVert W^j\rVert\le A b^j\) for all sufficiently large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
 T_W=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W^jH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^j
\]
converges, is positive definite because its first summand is \(H_0\succ0\), and satisfies
\[
 T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0.
\]
It is the unique solution: if \(D-WDW^{\mathsf T}=0\), then
\[
 \bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)\operatorname{vec}(D)=0,
\]
and \(\rho(W\otimes W)=\rho(W)^2<1\) makes the coefficient matrix invertible.  Put
\[
 E'=C_0-T_W\succ0,\qquad \mu'_0=m_0,
 \qquad x'= (I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0).
\]
The inverse in the last expression exists because \(\rho(W)<1\) implies \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)\).

The spectral-cut condition gives the real principal logarithm \(G'=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)\).  Indeed, on a complex Jordan block \(\lambda I+N\), with \(N^s=0\), the principal logarithm is
\[
 \operatorname{Log}(\lambda I+N)
 =\ell(\lambda)I+
 \sum_{q=1}^{s-1}\frac{(-1)^{q+1}}{q}\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}\right)^q,
 \qquad -\pi<\operatorname{Im}\ell(\lambda)<\pi.
\]
The finite nilpotent-series identities show that exponentiating this block returns \(\lambda I+N\).  Conjugate blocks have conjugate logarithms, so the logarithm of the real matrix \(W\) is real.  Since \(h>0\) by \(\text{ass:spacing}\), every eigenvalue \(g'\) of \(G'\) obeys
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(g')=h^{-1}\log|\lambda|<0,
 \qquad -\frac{\pi}{h}<\operatorname{Im}(g')<\frac{\pi}{h},
\]
using \(|\lambda|<1\) from \(\rho(W)<1\).  Thus \(G'\) satisfies \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).

Construct \(X'_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,T_W)\), set
\[
 X'_k=W^k(X'_0-x')+x'\qquad(k=0,1,2),
\]
and take mutually independent errors \(\varepsilon'_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E')\), independent of \(X'_0\).  This is a member of the deterministic Gaussian model specified by \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\), and \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\).  The definition of \(x'\) gives the affine intercept identity
\[
 (I_p-W)x'=m_1-Wm_0.
\]
Consequently the first mean step is \(m_1\), and the probe equation gives the second:
\[
 Wm_1+(I_p-W)x'
 =m_1+W(m_1-m_0)
 =m_1+Wd_0
 =m_1+d_1=m_2.
\]
For covariances, the Stein identity and the raw congruence give successively
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_0)+E'&=T_W+E'=C_0,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_1)+E'&=WT_WW^{\mathsf T}+E'=C_0-H_0=C_1,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_2)+E'&=W(T_W-H_0)W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=T_W-H_0-WH_0W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=C_0-H_0-H_1=C_2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All constructed variables are Gaussian, so equality of these means and covariances is equality of the three marginal laws.  Conversely, the covariance and mean recursions of every explanation in this model give \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\) and \(Wd_0=d_1\); stability and the alias strip give the first two filters, and uniqueness of the Stein solution gives \(T_W=\Sigma\) and \(C_0-T_W=E\succ0\).  Thus the strict-filter intersection is exactly the admissible transition fiber for the three laws.

It remains to verify local openness.  The spectral radius is continuous, and at a matrix whose spectrum avoids \(( -\infty,0]\), the finite spectrum has positive distance from that closed set; continuity of the roots of the characteristic polynomial therefore preserves both spectral conditions under a sufficiently small perturbation.  On the stable set,
\[
 \operatorname{vec}(T_W)
 =\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{vec}(H_0),
\]
which is continuous in \(W\).  Positive definiteness of \(C_0-T_W\) is open because its least eigenvalue is positive and continuous.  The admissible set is consequently relatively open in the torsor \(\mathcal F_3\), and every local branch through an admissible point has the torsor dimension computed above.

Because \(H_0^{-1/2}\) is invertible, \(d_0\ne0\) is equivalent to \(r=1\), whereas \(d_0=0\) is equivalent to \(r=0\).  In the latter case the norm certificate is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), because \(H_1^{-1/2}\) is invertible.  Hence the local dimension is \((p-1)(p-2)/2>0\) for \(d_0\ne0\) and \(p\ge3\), and it is \(p(p-1)/2>0\) for \(d_0=0\) and \(p\ge2\).  Moreover, stability implies \(I_p-V\) is invertible and the model mean formula gives
\[
 d_0=(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
Thus \(d_0=0\) is exactly the lower-dimensional equilibrium-mean locus \(\mu_0=x^\star\), while \(d_0\ne0\) is generic in the mean parameter.  Finally, if a larger unknown-common-noise model contains this deterministic Gaussian class, every pair or continuum of explanations constructed above remains a pair or continuum in the larger class and has the same three observed laws.  Identification in the larger class would imply identification in every subclass, so the displayed subclass witnesses prove the asserted converse transfer.

proposed.statement:
With only snapshots \(k=0,1,2\), if \(p\ge3\) and \(d_0
e0\), every admissible explanation lies in a local fiber of dimension \((p-1)(p-2)/2\). With four snapshots, \(\det K_0
e0\) implies the rational recovery identity \(V=K_1K_0^{-1}\); the condition \(\det K_0
e0\) holds outside a proper algebraic subset of the admissible parameter domain. Thus three snapshots are generically locally nonidentifying for \(p\ge3\), whereas four snapshots generically identify \(V\) and the full explanation whenever the unique recovered candidate passes the admissibility filters.
proposed.justification: The exact three-snapshot norm certificate and stabilizer dimension isolate the fourth destructive snapshot as the generic identification resource created by unknown common measurement covariance.
proposed.gap: Known-state-covariance results do not cover the shared unknown additive covariance: after differencing, three-snapshot compatibility leaves an \(O(p-1)\) fiber generically and an \(O(p)\) fiber at zero mean displacement, while the fourth snapshot supplies the second congruence needed by the rational Krylov map.
proposed.consumer: Experimental designers obtain an observable population certificate for three-snapshot compatibility and a sharp reason to collect a fourth destructive snapshot when a common covariance calibration sample is unavailable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the exact three-snapshot classification as a load-bearing dependency and expose the Gaussian and independence premises used by its structural-explanation construction; the claim text itself is unchanged.

prose_updates.tldr: Four independent Gaussian snapshots can identify a stable continuous-time linear mechanism even when every observed covariance contains the same unknown positive-definite measurement component, but the answer is a stratified fiber rather than automatically one matrix. With three snapshots, raw compatibility holds exactly when \(\lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2\); the compatible transitions form an \(O(p-1)\) torsor when \(d_0\ne0\) and an \(O(p)\) torsor when \(d_0=0\), giving continuous ambiguity generically for \(p\ge3\) and already at \(p=2\) on the zero-displacement elbow. A fourth snapshot identifies generically through the rational map \(K_1K_0^{-1}\), while stability, the principal-logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity decide structural compatibility. The same stabilizer dimension equals information nullity, finite fibers can contain exponentially many admissible branches, and regular branches admit perturbation bounds and Gaussian moment inference. Supplying \(E\) yields this paper's stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves model, not equality with that model class. Certified initialization and stable labeling of every noncyclic finite branch remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published snapshot-identification results either use supplied state covariances or work in broader known-noise transition models without classifying the fiber created by one unknown common additive covariance. In particular, a supplied \(E\) places the present stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise system inside the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves class, which also permits known process covariance, arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws; it does not make the two model classes equal.
project_justification.niche: Common measurement noise cancels from adjacent covariance differences but re-enters through level-covariance positivity. With three snapshots this gives an exactly computable one-vector orthogonal matching problem, including a zero-displacement \(O(p)\) elbow, while the fourth snapshot adds a second congruence that generically collapses the stabilizer through a rational Krylov identity.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the exact three-snapshot norm certificate and \(O(p-r)\) classification, an if-and-only-if four-snapshot block Gram certificate, a bijective admissibility map, complete exceptional and exponential-fiber results, rational perturbation theory, and branchwise inference. It also identifies the precise supplied-noise subclass relation and retains certified global initialization and branch labeling as the remaining open construction problem.

prose_updates.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest congruence architecture. Its published class allows known process covariance \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws. After a supplied measurement covariance \(E\) is subtracted, the model studied here is only its stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, \(Q=0\) subclass; the inherited consequence used here is the consecutive latent-covariance congruence, not equality of model classes or an exact reduction to every part of their theorem. WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer. QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains neither an unknown common additive covariance nor the exact three-snapshot norm and stabilizer classification proved here. MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrödinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate. Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered. KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the regular-stratum results. KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime from destructive marginal snapshots.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact population conditions--spectral matching, block Gram equality, and the three-snapshot whitened norm equality--must not be imposed as empirical accept-or-reject equalities, because unconstrained noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero. On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is the off-model rational estimator used by the perturbation theorem. The radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full plug-in reconstruction is defined, whereas the smaller radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) also preserves the stability, logarithm, Stein, and reconstructed-covariance positivity filters; neither radius forces noisy moments onto the exact population fiber. On a noncyclic finite stratum, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is a population-branch-centered residual estimator, not a globally implementable branch finder until certified initialization and labeling are solved. The two structural plug-ins are \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) and \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\), each with initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat m_0\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact population three-snapshot norm certificate, its \(O(p-r)\) fibers, the generic four-snapshot frontier, stabilizer dimension, achieved exponential multiplicity, information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and local regular-branch limit law are theorem-level deliverables. The \(d_0=0\) elbow has continuous \(O(p)\) ambiguity already at \(p=2\); when \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the raw fiber is only zero-dimensional and admissibility filters may leave one or more isolated candidates. Any unknown-common-noise supermodel containing the deterministic Gaussian subclass inherits its three-snapshot nonidentification witnesses. Supplying \(E\) gives only the stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022; the broader published class also permits known \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time transitions, and non-Gaussian finite-second-moment laws. The global certified initializer, complete branch certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open. No uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps, and exact population equalities are not empirical testing rules.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_4(E)\) be the set of transition matrices occurring in structural explanations of the four observed marginal laws with the supplied covariance \(E\), subject to \(\text{ass:spacing}\), \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\), \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\), and \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\).  This is proof notation for a causal-model compatibility set; it is not a definition of the observable identifying functional.  We first prove
\[
\mathcal C_4(E)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E).
\]

For necessity, take \(W\in\mathcal C_4(E)\), and write \(L_k=\operatorname{Cov}(X_k)\).  By \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\), and \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\),
\[
 \mathbb E[X_k]=W^k(\mu_0-x^\star)+x^\star,
 \qquad
 L_k=W^k\Sigma(W^{\mathsf T})^k.
\]
Because \(W=\exp(hG)\) is invertible and \(\Sigma\succ0\), congruence by \(W^k\) gives \(L_k\succ0\) for every \(k\in K\).  The errors have mean zero by \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), and their independence from \(X_0\), hence from each deterministic \(X_k\), follows from \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\).  Therefore
\[
 m_k=\mathbb E[X_k],
 \qquad
 C_k=L_k+E,
 \qquad
 \widetilde C_k=C_k-E=L_k\succ0.
\]
The deterministic covariance recursion and the affine mean formula now yield, for every index for which the displayed objects exist,
\[
 W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\quad(k=0,1,2),
 \qquad
 d_k=W^k(W-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star),
\]
and hence
\[
 Wd_0=d_1,
 \qquad
 Wd_1=d_2.
\]

We next verify the filters in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\).  On a complex Jordan block of \(hG\) with eigenvalue \(hg\), exponentiation produces the eigenvalue \(e^{hg}\).  Thus \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(h>0\) from \(\text{ass:spacing}\) give
\[
 \rho(W)=\max_{g\in\operatorname{spec}(G)}e^{h\operatorname{Re}(g)}<1.
\]
If \(e^{hg}\) were a negative real number, then \(h\operatorname{Im}(g)\) would equal \((2\ell+1)\pi\) for some integer \(\ell\), which is impossible under \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\); exponentials are nonzero.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing.
\]
The common covariance cancels from the first adjacent difference:
\[
 H_0=C_0-C_1=L_0-L_1=L_0-WL_0W^{\mathsf T}.
\]
If \(D-WDW^{\mathsf T}=0\), vectorization gives
\[
 \bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)\operatorname{vec}(D)=0.
\]
Every eigenvalue of \(W\otimes W\) is a product of two eigenvalues of \(W\), so its spectral radius is \(\rho(W)^2<1\).  Consequently \(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\) is invertible, and the Stein equation has at most one solution.  Since \(L_0\) is a solution, the reconstruction in the frozen definition satisfies
\[
 T_W=L_0=\widetilde C_0,
 \qquad
 E_W=C_0-T_W=C_0-\widetilde C_0=E.
\]
All restrictions in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\) hold, proving \(\mathcal C_4(E)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\).

For sufficiency, take \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\), and define
\[
 \Sigma=widetilde C_0,
 \qquad
 \mu_0=m_0,
 \qquad
 b=m_1-Wm_0.
\]
Membership in the fiber gives \(\Sigma\succ0\) and \(\rho(W)<1\).  In particular, \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)\), so \(I_p-W\) is invertible and
\[
 x^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}b
\]
is well defined.  Since \(b=(I_p-W)x^\star\), the affine recursion beginning at \(m_0\) gives \(m_1\) at its first step.  The two probe restrictions then give successively
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Wm_1+b
 &=m_1+W(m_1-m_0)
 =m_1+Wd_0
 =m_1+d_1=m_2,\\
 Wm_2+b
 &=m_2+W(m_2-m_1)
 =m_2+Wd_1
 =m_2+d_2=m_3.
 \end{aligned}
\]

The spectral-cut condition permits the principal logarithm.  More explicitly, on a complex Jordan block \(J=\lambda I+N\), where \(N^s=0\) and \(-\pi<\operatorname{Arg}(\lambda)<\pi\), set
\[
 \operatorname{Log}(J)
 =\bigl(\log|\lambda|+i\operatorname{Arg}(\lambda)\bigr)I
 +\sum_{r=1}^{s-1}\frac{(-1)^{r+1}}{r}\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}\right)^r.
\]
The finite nilpotent logarithm and exponential series are inverse under composition, so exponentiating this block returns \(J\).  Conjugate blocks receive conjugate logarithms; pairing them in a real canonical form shows that \(\operatorname{Log}(W)\) is real.  Its eigenvalues are the scalar principal logarithms of the eigenvalues of \(W\).  Therefore
\[
 G_W=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)
\]
is real and satisfies
\[
 \exp(hG_W)=W,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{spec}(G_W)
 =h^{-1}\log|\operatorname{spec}(W)|<0,
 \qquad
 -\frac{\pi}{h}<\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{spec}(G_W)<\frac{\pi}{h}.
\]
Thus it satisfies \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).  Conversely, if \(L\) is any real logarithm of \(W\) whose spectrum lies in the open strip \(-\pi<\operatorname{Im}(z)<\pi\), the scalar identity \(\operatorname{Log}(e^z)=z\) is holomorphic on a neighborhood of \(\operatorname{spec}(L)\).  Composition of the corresponding convergent local power series on each generalized eigenspace gives
\[
 L=\operatorname{Log}(e^L)=\operatorname{Log}(W).
\]
Hence the open alias strip leaves no additional generator branch.

Construct \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,\Sigma)\), set \(X_k=W^k(X_0-x^\star)+x^\star\), and take mutually independent \(\varepsilon_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E)\), independent of \(X_0\).  This construction satisfies the stated Gaussian, independence, and zero-process-noise assumptions.  The preceding recursion gives \(\mathbb E[X_k]=m_k\).  The level congruences in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\) give inductively
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_k)
 =W^k\Sigma(W^{\mathsf T})^k
 =\widetilde C_k
 \qquad(k\in K).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E[X_k+\varepsilon_k]=m_k,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_k+\varepsilon_k)=\widetilde C_k+E=C_k.
\]
Both the constructed and observed marginal laws are nonsingular Gaussian laws, so equality of these moments is equality of laws.  Thus \(W\in\mathcal C_4(E)\), proving the reverse inclusion.  Moreover \(E_W=E\succ0\) by \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\); fixing this residual is strictly stronger than merely requiring \(C_0-T_W\succ0\).

Now retain only snapshots \(0,1,2\).  The same calculations show that their covariance and mean consequences are precisely
\[
 W\widetilde C_0W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_1,
 \qquad
 W\widetilde C_1W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_2,
 \qquad
 Wd_0=d_1.
\]
Conversely, these three equations, together with \(\widetilde C_k\succ0\), reproduce the three latent moment recursions after setting \(b=m_1-Wm_0\); the remaining stability, logarithm, Stein, and supplied-noise equality restrictions are what distinguish the present structural subclass.

By \(\text{lem:aalto-model-scope}\), the published full-state moment recursion is
\[
 P_{j+1}=AP_jA^{\mathsf T}+Q,
 \qquad
 \bar m_{j+1}=A\bar m_j+b.
\]
Setting \(A=W\), \(P_j=\widetilde C_j\), \(Q=0\), and \(b=(I_p-W)x^\star\) maps every present noise-subtracted equation into that recursion.  The implication is only equation-level: the cited model directly observes its state, whereas the present model observes a Gaussian state plus a supplied common measurement error.  It is also a strict inclusion.  For example, the cited recursion allows the invertible choice \(A=2I_p\), \(Q=0\), and any positive-definite initial covariance; this choice is excluded here because its spectral radius is \(2\), while every \(W=\exp(hG)\) allowed by \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) has spectral radius below one.  The cited scope further allows known nonzero \(Q\), imposes no principal-logarithm embedding condition, and, by \(\text{lem:aalto-model-scope}\), does not require Gaussian laws once finite second moments exist.  This proves the asserted strict subclass relation and shows why no equality with the published observation-model class follows.

Finally, we derive the finite sign map rather than importing it.  Define the positive-definite whitened matrices and the whitened transition
\[
 R_0=\widetilde C_0^{-1/2}\widetilde C_1\widetilde C_0^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 R_1=\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}\widetilde C_2\widetilde C_1^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 U=\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}W\widetilde C_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first covariance equation is equivalent to \(UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\), and substitution into the second gives
\[
 UR_0U^{\mathsf T}=R_1.
\]
Suppose that \(R_0\) and \(R_1\) have the same simple ordered spectrum.  Choose orthogonal eigendecompositions
\[
 R_0=P\Lambda P^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 R_1=Q_1\Lambda Q_1^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p),
\]
where \(\lambda_i\ne\lambda_j\) for \(i\ne j\).  Then \(D=Q_1^{\mathsf T}UP\) is orthogonal and satisfies \(D\Lambda D^{\mathsf T}=\Lambda\), equivalently \(D\Lambda=\Lambda D\).  Entrywise,
\[
 (\lambda_j-\lambda_i)D_{ij}=0.
\]
Simplicity therefore makes \(D\) diagonal, and orthogonality gives \(D_{ii}\in\{-1,1\}\).  Hence every covariance-compatible transition belongs to the explicit list
\[
 W_D=\widetilde C_1^{1/2}Q_1DP^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_0^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),
 \qquad
 s_i\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
There are at most \(2^p\) such candidates.  Put
\[
 a=P^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_0^{-1/2}d_0,
 \qquad
 c=Q_1^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}d_1.
\]
The mean equation \(Wd_0=d_1\) is equivalent to \(Da=c\).  If every \(a_i\ne0\), each sign is forced by the computable ratio
\[
 s_i=\frac{c_i}{a_i},
\]
and compatibility requires every such ratio to belong to \(\{-1,1\}\).  For four-snapshot compatibility one additionally tests
\[
 W_D\widetilde C_2W_D^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_3,
 \qquad
 W_Dd_1=d_2.
\]
Testing the survivors also against \(\rho(W_D)<1\), the negative-real spectral cut, the Stein equation, and \(E_{W_D}=E\) gives exactly the members of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\), because this list exhausts the first two covariance congruences and every remaining test is one of the defining restrictions.  This completes both the exact known-noise reduction within the present model and the finite sign classification, without asserting equality with the broader published class.

added_lemmas.statement: Section 2 of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 studies, in a locally denoted dimension \(n\), the exactly observed full-state recursion \(Z_j=A Z_{j-1}+b+\eta_{j-1}\), where the process innovations have known covariance \(Q\) and the temporal orthogonality specified there.  Its moment equations are \(\bar m_j=A\bar m_{j-1}+b\) and \(P_j=AP_{j-1}A^{\mathsf T}+Q\).  Theorem 2.1 assumes that \(A\) is invertible but imposes neither stability nor continuous-time embeddability, and the paragraph immediately following its proof states that finite second moments, rather than Gaussianity, suffice for these moment equations and the stated identification argument.

source.verbatim_statement: This is not required, but it suffices that the initial state and noise distributions have finite second moments.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose that the common measurement covariance \(E\) is supplied, and set \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\).  Within the present stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise structural model, the transition fiber compatible with the four observed marginal laws is exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\).  Its covariance restrictions are \(W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\) for \(k=0,1,2\), and its residual-noise restriction is the equality \(E_W=E\), equivalently \(C_0-E-T_W=0\), rather than only the unknown-noise inequality \(C_0-T_W\succ0\).  With only snapshots \(k=0,1,2\), the covariance and affine-mean consequences are exactly \(W\widetilde C_0W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_1\), \(W\widetilde C_1W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_2\), and \(Wd_0=d_1\).  Under the identification of the published discrete transition with \(W\), its state covariances with \(\widetilde C_k\), and its known process covariance with \(Q=0\), these are an equation-level subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1.  The inclusion is strict at model scope: their full-state system permits a known nonzero process covariance, an invertible discrete-time transition without stability or continuous-time embeddability restrictions, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws, whereas it has no measurement-error layer.  Thus only the displayed moment-equation consequence, not equality of observation-model classes, is inherited.  If the two three-snapshot whitened congruence invariants have the same simple spectrum and every source probe coordinate is nonzero, the three-snapshot equations are computably reduced to at most \(2^p\) sign candidates.  The candidates for \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\) are then tested against the remaining fourth-snapshot congruence and probe equation and against the stability, principal-logarithm, Stein, and equality \(E_W=E\) filters.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current comparison can be read as an exact reduction to the full published model.  After supplied-noise subtraction, only the moment equations embed, with the published process covariance specialized to \(Q=0\); stability, principal-log embeddability, Gaussianity, and zero process noise make the present equation system a strict subclass, while the observation models remain different.
